title: Affordable housing and public policy
text:
This is a critical issue that will again be at the center of our local and national politics. Issue is who has the best ideas and will to execute? This is a major failing in coastal and "blue" districts!

Surprised this nice summary did not mention building techniques that are scalable using a factory model (i.e. modular construction) rather than being "stick built" from scratch on site. This has been happening in some countries. Need to encourage and incentivize innovation, in addition to zoning issues discussed.  It is interesting that building high end condos can also contribute to affordable housing by downstream effects!  We also need to rethink the notion of a starter place to live (i.e. home) as a way to build wealth and address tax strategies that only favor home ownership, rather than on rental. Why can't housing cost broadly be deductible, which would be less regressive and benefit lower income renters as well?

Here is an interesting experiment going on in Denver to convert vacant office buildings into housing:  https://www.wsj.com/real-estate/commercial/america-s-emptiest-downtown-f1f4cdf1?st=VRNwA5&reflink=desktopwebshare_permalink
